note: Berendes/Beck: Illyrian orris; sword-like leaves, variously coloured flowers, fragrant rhizome. Exact species debated (I. germanica/pallida).
Berendes/Gunther: sweet flag; iris-like narrow leaves, knotty aromatic creeping rhizome. Some propose Iris pseudacorus.
Standard identification; Linnaean epithet derives from Dioscorides' 'Athamantic meon'.
Leek-like leaves, triangular stem, black fragrant olive-like tubers; C. rotundus or C. longus per Berendes/Beck.
Indian 'cyperus' like ginger, saffron-yellow and bitter when chewed: turmeric (Berendes, Beck).
Traditional identification as cardamom; stated origins (Commagene, Armenia) make the ancient source debated.
Indian and 'Syrian' nard are both spikenard rhizomes traded via different routes (Berendes, Beck).
Alpine 'saliunca' of Liguria and Istria: Valeriana celtica (standard).
Berendes: Valeriana tuberosa; black fragrant asphodel-like root tubers. Description defective (no flower), so debated.
Ivy-like rounded leaves, flower between leaves at root, fragrant rootlets: asarabacca (standard).
Pontic valerian with fetid nard-like root; Linnaeus named V. phu after it; V. dioscoridis also proposed.
Malabathrum leaf of Indian trade is generally identified with Cinnamomum tamala; Dioscorides' account partly fabulous.
Aromatic bark traded via Arabia; usually equated with Chinese cassia (syn. C. cassia); ancient source debated.
Several trade grades of cinnamon; identity of ancient cinnamomum versus modern cinnamon remains debated.
Woody cluster-like aromatic from Armenia/Media/Pontus; identity long disputed, genus Amomum conventional.
Arabian, Indian and Syrian costus: aromatic root of costus (standard; syn. Saussurea costus, S. lappa).
Aromatic rush from Libya/Arabia/Nabataea used in unguents; camel grass per Berendes/Beck.
Traditionally sweet flag; jointed culm with cobweb-like pith suggests an Indian aromatic grass. Debated.
Judaean balsam tree (opobalsamum, xylobalsamum, carpobalsamum): Commiphora gileadensis (standard).
Spiny woody shrub of Nisyros/Rhodes/Syria used by perfumers; spiny broom often proposed, identity uncertain.
Fragrant growth on cedar, white poplar and oak: epiphytic lichens (Berendes: Usnea, Parmelia).
Fragrant spotted wood from India/Arabia used as incense: agarwood (syn. Aquilaria agallocha).
Unidentified Indian aromatic bark resembling mulberry-fig bark; no secure identification.
Unidentified myrrh-like tear of an Arabian tree used as incense; source not securely identified.
Multi-ingredient Egyptian temple incense compound; no single source taxon.
Corycian saffron stigmas; standard identification.
Pressed residue of saffron unguent (multi-ingredient); mapped to eponymous saffron.
Standard identification (Berendes, Beck); large rough leaves, yellow flowers, aromatic root.
Crateuas' Egyptian prostrate seaside herb with lentil-like leaves; no accepted identification.
Olive oil, especially omphacinum from unripe olives.
Sweet thick exudate from olive trunks at Palmyra per Dioscorides; nature of the product uncertain.
Oil pressed from kroton (castor) seeds; standard.
Oil of bitter almonds (metopion); syn. Prunus dulcis.
Oil of balanos myrepsike (ben nut), generally Moringa peregrina.
Oil from white henbane seed; white seed indicates Hyoscyamus albus.
Cnidian berry (kokkos knidios) is the fruit of Daphne gnidium (standard).
Oil from radish seed.
Oil from mustard seed; ancient sinapi includes white and black mustard.
Oil from tender leaves of black myrtle.
Oil from ripe laurel berries.
Oil from ripe fruit of schinos (lentisk).
Oil made from mastic resin of lentisk.
Rose petals steeped in oil with aromatic stypsis; rose species not specified.
Elate here likely the date-palm spathe (cf. Diosc. 1.109, astringent like rose oil); fir less likely.
Oil perfumed by quinces (kydonia mela) laid over it.
Oil of oenanthe, the fragrant flower of the (wild) grapevine.
Fenugreek (telis) oil with calamus and cyperus.
Multi-herb oil named after sampsuchon (marjoram); mapped to eponymous ingredient.
Oil steeped with basil (okimon) leaves.
Oil of abrotonon (southernwood); species-level identity of abrotonon slightly debated.
Oil steeped with dill flowers.
Susinum/leirinon: oil of white lily flowers with aromatics.
Oil perfumed with narcissus flowers; species uncertain.
Oil perfumed with saffron.
Oil of kypros flowers (henna), standard identification.
Oil perfumed with Illyrian iris root.
Multi-ingredient oil prepared with grape must; mapped to eponymous ingredient.
Amarakon equals sampsuchon (marjoram) per Diosc. 3.39; multi-ingredient unguent.
Egyptian multi-ingredient unguent named for galbanum (metopion tree); mapped to galbanum source.
Oily fraction of fresh myrrh.
Multi-ingredient unguent named after cinnamon; ancient cinnamon identity debated.
Multi-ingredient unguent named after spikenard.
Unguent like nardinum with malabathrum leaf; mapped to eponymous ingredient.
Gum-resin of an Arabian thorny tree: myrrh (standard).
Cut root of an unnamed Boeotian tree smelling of myrrh; unidentified.
Resin of a quince-like tree from Pisidia/Cilicia: Styrax officinalis (standard).
Sea urchin (Echinoidea, e.g. Paracentrotus lividus).
Land hedgehog (Erinaceus).
Seahorse (Hippocampus), burnt to ash.
Purple-dye murex shells (Muricidae), burnt.
Pontic mussels (probably Mytilus), burnt; acts like whelks (kerykes).
Small bivalves (probably Donax trunculus).
Opercula (lids) of purple-dye snails.
Operculum of a shellfish from Indian lakes; the later 'blatta byzantina' incense.
Land snail (Helix and allies).
Freshwater crabs (Potamon), burnt to ash.
Land scorpion, applied to its own sting.
Sea scorpion: scorpionfish (Scorpaena), gall used.
Sea dragon: weever fish (Trachinus draco), applied to its own sting.
Marine 'centipede', probably a bristle worm (Polychaeta); uncertain.
Torpedo ray applied for chronic headache.
Viper flesh (Vipera spp.).
Shed skin of snakes.
Sea hare, like a small squid: probably Aplysia.
Land hare (Lepus europaeus): brain, rennet etc.
Stingray spine (Dasyatis pastinaca).
Cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis): ink, cuttlebone.
Red mullet (Mullus).
Dried hippopotamus testicle against snakebite.
Beaver (Castor fiber) 'testicle', i.e. castoreum sacs.
Domestic weasel (probably Mustela nivalis), dried and burnt.
Frogs boiled as antidote to reptile bites.
Silurus: catfish (Silurus glanis or Nile catfish).
Salted picarel (Spicara smaris), head burnt.
Maenis (Spicara maena), head burnt.
Fresh goby (Gobiidae).
Salted tuna flesh (Thunnus thynnus).
Fermented fish/meat brine sauce; animal-derived preparation.
Broth of young fish; animal-derived preparation.
Bed bugs (Cimex lectularius).
Many-footed creatures under water jars that roll up: woodlice (Oniscidea).
Silphe found in bakeries: probably cockroach (Blatta orientalis).
Sea lung: a jellyfish (e.g. Rhizostoma pulmo).
Lungs of pig, lamb and bear applied to chafing.
Dried fox lung for asthma; fox fat.
Roasted donkey liver for epilepsy.
Male red deer genitals against viper bites.
Burnt donkey hooves.
Horny callosities on horses' legs (chestnuts).
Burnt goat hooves for alopecia.
Juice of roasted goat liver for night blindness.
Wild boar liver against reptile bites.
Liver of the rabid dog eaten against hydrophobia.
Burnt old leather from shoes; animal-derived.
Domestic hens split open and applied warm.
Hen's egg (yolk, white, shell).
Roasted cicadas for bladder pains.
Locusts/grasshoppers fumigated.
Bird called ossifragus by Romans: probably bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus).
Small bird with peacock-like crest: crested lark (Galerida cristata).
Diving seabird (shearwater, cormorant or duck); uncertain.
Swallow chicks (Hirundo rustica).
Ivory filings (elephant tusk).
Burnt pig astragalus.
Burnt and washed red deer antler.
Caterpillars on vegetables (probably cabbage white larvae).
Cantharides from wheat: blister beetles (Meloidae, e.g. Mylabris, Lytta).
Spotted lizard-like animal: fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra).
Spider called holkos or lykos: probably a wolf spider (Lycosidae).
Lizard head and blood.
Seps 'Chalcidic lizard' (Chalcides); chapter text also contains skink (Scincus scincus, ch. 66).
Earthworms (Lumbricidae) applied to severed sinews.
Shrew (Crocidura), applied to its own bite.
House mice (Mus musculus) split open.
Milk in general (cow, goat, sheep, ass, etc.).
Fresh and aged cheese; dairy preparation.
Butter from the fattest milk; dairy preparation.
Unwashed sheep's wool.
Fat extracted from greasy wool: crude lanolin.
Rennet of the hare.
Fats of goose, hen, pig, bear, etc.
Bone marrow of deer, calf, bull, goat, sheep.
Animal gall/bile and its storage.
Blood of goose, kid, duck, pigeon, etc.
Dung of grazing cattle; chapter covers other dungs.
Human urine (and other urines).
Bee honey (Apis mellifera product); Attic Hymettian best.
Beeswax (Apis mellifera product).
Bee glue (Apis mellifera product).
Pyros: free-threshing wheat; bread and durum wheat not distinguished in the text.
Barley (standard); includes barley water (ptisane).
Beer made from barley.
Barley drink used instead of wine (Iberia, Britain).

alternatives: Triticum turgidum subsp. dicoccum;Triticum aestivum subsp. spelta
note: Two kinds: 'simple' (one grain, einkorn) and 'dikokkos' (two grains per husk, emmer).
Coarse meal of zea and wheat; porridge base.
Same kind as zea but less nourishing; hulled wheat, usually emmer or einkorn.
Gruel of finely ground zea: hulled wheat, emmer (T. turgidum subsp. dicoccum) or spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta); debated.
Groats like chondros but chaffier, from zea: emmer or spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta); debated.
Bromos: reed-like cereal with wheat-like leaves and nodes; standard identification oat.
Cereal of marshy places; rice, uncontroversial.
Groats from 'dikokkos zea', i.e. two-grained emmer (T. turgidum subsp. dicoccum); spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta) possible.
Kenchros = common millet; standard identification.
Elymos/meline, a millet-like cereal; usually identified as foxtail millet.
Sesamon = sesame; uncontroversial.
Aira growing among wheat = darnel; standard identification.

headword: ἄμμλον ὠνόμασται διὰ τὸ χωρὶς μύλου κατασκευάζεσθαι
note: Starch made without milling from 'setanios' wheat by soaking and treading; soft wheat assumed.
Meal of telis (synonyms boukeras, aigokeras) = fenugreek; uncontroversial.
Linosperm (flax seed), same virtues as fenugreek; uncontroversial.
Erebinthos hemeros = cultivated chickpea; uncontroversial.
Kyamos Hellenikos = Greek (broad) bean; uncontroversial.
Spongy silphium-like 'root'; standard identification larch polypore (Berendes: Lärchenschwamm).
Rha from beyond the Bosporus; Berendes 'Rhapontik'; exact Rheum species debated.
Named after Illyrian king Gentius; Berendes Enzian; standard G. lutea.
Round (female), long (male), klematitis kinds: A. rotunda, A. longa L. (GBIF: A. fontanesii), A. clematitis.
Sweet root; burr-like fruit heads described fit G. echinata; G. glabra usual identification.
Walnut-like leaves, tall stem, red root; standard Centaurea centaurium (now Rhaponticoides).
Small centaury, hypericum-like, of moist places; uncontroversial.
Ixine birdlime found at the roots; standard Atractylis (Carlina) gummifera.
Berendes: Carthamus corymbosus L. (= Cardopatium corymbosum); umbel-like spiny inflorescence, black root.
Like black chamaeleon, cress-scented root; Berendes Carduus pycnocephalus; tentative.
Leaf-cups collecting water; Berendes Dipsacus silvestris (= D. fullonum).
Sea-urchin-like spiny head, purple flowers; Berendes Cnicus ferox (= Cirsium/Lophiolepis ferox), others Cnicus acarna; uncertain.
Berendes: not determined; Sprengel tentatively Onopordon arabicum; only virtues given.
Spiny head, edible root and shoots; Berendes S. maculatus; artichoke rejected.

Cobweb-like down gathered as wool; Berendes Onopordon acanthium (perhaps O. illyricum).
Akanthos/paideros of gardens, broad glossy leaves; standard A. mollis.
Berendes Ononis antiquorum (now O. spinosa subsp. antiquorum).
Only cyperus-like bitter root described; Sprengel Cirsium tuberosum, Fraas Centaurea dalmatica.
Spiny shrub whose cut root yields gum tragacanth; Berendes: Astragalus species.
Spiny plant with edible young leaves; standard E. campestre.
Squill-like fleshy leaves, bitter juice from India/Arabia; A. vera usual, Socotrine A. perryi possible.
Pontic/Cappadocian wormwood; chapter adds seriphon (sea wormwood).
Male and female kinds; male usually A. abrotanum, female debated.
Not described; Sprengel/Fraas Origanum syriacum/smyrnaeum, Lenz Hyssopus officinalis (rare in Greece).
From the Stoechades islands off Marseille; Berendes L. stoechas.
Berendes Origanum heracleoticum (= O. vulgare subsp. hirtum).
Whiter, more hyssop-like leaves; usual O. onites; Berendes 'Origanum creticum'.
Berendes Origanum vulgare var. album; dill-like umbels, white flowers.
Sticky broad-leaved kind: Sprengel Stachys glutinosa; slender kind Satureja juliana (Fraas); uncertain.
Glechon, well-known herb; uncontroversial.
Cretan herb like pennyroyal; chapter adds pseudodiktamnon.
Elelisphakon: long shrub, square twigs, rough whitish fragrant leaves; Greek sage.

Berendes Satureja capitata (= Thymbra capitata); purple capitate heads.

Garden creeping kind and erect wild kind (zygis); Berendes Thymus serpyllum, T. glabratus.
Sampsuchon/amarakon of Cyzicus and Cyprus; Berendes Origanum majorana.
Saffron-coloured fragrant Attic kind; Berendes Melilotus creticus, M. neapolitanus; Sprengel M. officinalis.

note: Mint-like, broader-leaved, fragrant; usual identification water mint (Berendes 'Wasserminze').

Basil-like, hairier, fragrant; Berendes Thymus acinos (= Clinopodium acinos).
Berendes: undetermined; Fraas Gnaphalium sanguineum; cinnamon-scented root.
Garden, mountain and wild rue; garden R. graveolens/chalepensis, mountain kind R. montana.

Grass-like leaves, milk-white flowers, small bulb; Berendes lists Allium nigrum/magicum; contested.

Fennel-like rough leaves, golden umbels; Berendes Echinophora tenuifolia.
Pelion plant, marjoram-like leaves, golden flower; Fraas Hypericum olympicum; others Inula, Helianthemum.

Wild staphylinos with central purple floret; Berendes Daucus carota var. silvestris.
Massilian = Seseli tortuosum; Ethiopian = Bupleurum fruticosum; Peloponnesian uncertain (Berendes).
Cretan seseli of Amanus; round double shield-shaped seed; Berendes T. officinale.
Syrian celery-like black seed; traditional identification Sison amomum.
Anison; uncontroversial.
Karo, known aromatic seed; standard caraway.
Anethon; uncontroversial.
Cultivated kyminon (Ethiopian 'royal' cumin); Berendes Cuminum cyminum.
Small plant with 5-6 round heads; Sprengel and Fraas Lagoecia cuminoides.

headword: ἐστι δὲ καὶ ἕτερον γένος ἀγρίου κυμίνου
note: Horn-like capsules with nigella-like seed; Sprengel N. arvensis, Fraas N. aristata (= N. arvensis subsp. aristata).
Tiny oregano-tasting seed; Sprengel Ammi copticum (= ajowan), Fraas Ammi visnaga.
Korion; uncontroversial.
Garden selinon; uncontroversial.
Rock/mountain umbellifer; Gesner and Sprengel Seseli libanotis, Fraas Seseli annuum.

Hipposelinon/olusatrum, black seed; Fraas Smyrnium olusatrum.

Marathon; uncontroversial.

Three kinds: Cretan = Athamanta cretensis; second Peucedanum cervaria (= Cervaria rivini); third Ammi majus (Fraas).

Burning root for toothache; Berendes Anacyclus pyrethrum; 'umbel' wording questioned.

Plane-like leaves, broad winged seeds; Berendes Bärenklau (Heracleum).
Narthex pith; uncontroversial.
Peukedanon; Berendes Haarstrang (Peucedanum).
Melanthion; uncontroversial.

Juice of Syrian plant with horned-poppy leaves; Berendes 'ohne Zweifel' Glaucium corniculatum.
Fish glue from the belly of a large Pontic fish, i.e. sturgeon swim bladder.
Birdlime from round berries of ixia with box-like leaves, i.e. mistletoe.
Rough clinging stems, whorled leaves; Berendes Galium aparine.
Double shield-like silicles; Sprengel/Fraas Farsetia clypeata (= Fibigia clypeata).

Safflower-like thistle used as spindle; Matthiolus/Fraas Carthamus lanatus.

Bed-foot-like whorled flowers; Berendes Clinopodium vulgare.
Sprengel Leontice leontopetalum; Fraas Roemeria hybrida (pods, red flower) — debated.
Teukrion of Cilicia, chamaedrys-like; Berendes Teucrium flavum.
Oak-like small leaves; Sprengel/Sibthorp T. chamaedrys, Fraas T. lucidum.
Fragmentary chapter; Berendes only conjectures: Sprengel Lamium maculatum, Fraas Lamium striatum.
Garland lychnis, purple leukoion-like flower; Berendes Lychnis coronaria.
Wild lychnis similar to garden one; Berendes Agrostemma githago.
Krinon/leirion, garland flower, source of susinon oil; uncontroversial.
Ballote/melamprasion, square black stems; Berendes Ballota.
Melissophyllon, loved by bees; uncontroversial.
Prasion; Berendes Marrubium vulgare.
Like prasion but longer, whiter leaves; Berendes Stachys germanica (Sibthorp S. palaestina).
Lapathon-like leaves with sori beneath; Berendes Scolopendrium officinale.
Lily-like white flower, black seed; Dodonaeus Anthericum ramosum, Fraas Lloydia graeca; uncertain.
Triphyllon/asphaltion smelling of bitumen; Berendes Asphaltklee.
Polion/teuthrion, white small shrub; standard Teucrium polium.
Skordion of marshy places, garlic-like smell; Berendes Knoblauch-Gamander.
Bechion, cough herb, smoke inhaled; Berendes Tussilago farfara.
Seaside wormwood-like shrub; Berendes A. arborescens and A. campestris; single-stemmed kind uncertain.
Sprengel and Fraas Ambrosia maritima; rue-like leaves, Cappadocian garlands.
Botrys, yellowish fragrant herb; Berendes Chenopodium botrys.
Round sweet edible root; Berendes Geranium tuberosum; second kind Erodium malacoides.
White soft leaves used as stuffing; Berendes Athanasia maritima (= Otanthus maritimus).
Typhe of marshes with dense fluffy spike; Berendes Typha angustifolia.
Berendes: not determined; Anguillara Cynanchum nigrum, Lobelius Circaea lutetiana.
Root with many round heads; Fraas Spiraea filipendula, Sprengel Pedicularis tuberosa.
Greater konyza; Berendes Erigeron viscosum; small kind E. graveolens; third Inula britannica.
Lily-like, leek-green leaves, yellow flowers; Berendes: not determined; Hemerocallis fulva or Lilium bulbiferum.

headword: λευκόϊον γνώριμον. ἐστι δʼ αὐτοῦ διαφορὰ ἐν τῷ ἄνθει
note: Leukoion; yellow kind used medicinally = Cheiranthus cheiri (Berendes); other colours Matthiola.
Wheat-like leaves, millet-like seed; Fraas Crucianella monspeliaca, Sprengel Polygonum persicaria.
Rock plant with thelygonon/arrhenogonon forms; Fraas Mercurialis perennis; Sprengel M. tomentosa.
Kynos orchis with paired tubers; Berendes Orchis papilionacea or O. morio.
Leek-like leaves, purple flowers; Sprengel declined, Fraas Orchis undulatifolia (= O. italica).
Three-leaved bulbous aphrodisiac; Fraas Aceras anthropophora, Sprengel Tulipa; erythronion part also undetermined.
Cultivated horminon, square stem; Berendes Salvia horminum (= S. viridis); wild kind other Salvia.

note: Hedysaron/pelekinos with axe-like seed; Berendes Coronilla securidaca (syn. Securigera securidaca).
Anchusa-like leaves; Fraas Onosma echioides; Sprengel wavered (Lithospermum/Anchusa).
White water lily; second nymphaia with yellow flower = Nuphar lutea (Berendes).

Crescent leaf like dracontion; Sprengel/Fraas Scolopendrium hemionitis (= Asplenium sagittatum).

Fennel-like leaves, large yellow 'ox-eye' flowers; Berendes Chrysanthemum coronarium.
Male peony with walnut-like leaves; female with divided leaves = P. officinalis.
Stony white seeds; standard Lithospermum officinale.
Zea-like stems, white millet-sized seed; Berendes Phalaris nodosa (= P. aquatica), Sprengel P. canariensis.
Red dye root, wild and cultivated kinds; standard identification (Berendes, Beck).

Fern like scolopendrion but rougher and more divided; holly fern traditional, uncertain.

Wild mallow with leaves cut like hiera botane; Berendes/Beck Malva alcea.
Rope-fibre plant with ash-like, ill-smelling leaves; uncontroversial.

Foetid shrub; name kept by Linnaean genus; standard identification.

Lentil-like leaves, purple flower, moist untilled ground; genus named from it, species uncertain.
Rue-like leaves, resin-scented black seed; Berendes H. crispum (=triquetrifolium); H. perforatum also proposed.
Larger hypericum, yellow flowers, fruit staining fingers blood-red; species uncertain.

Heath-like red leaves, called hypericum; H. coris named from it, H. empetrifolium fits Greece.
Creeping pine-scented herb; three kinds described: first A. chamaepitys, others subsp. chia and A. iva.
Roman vettonica named in the text; standard identification.
Dark, hairy, astringent dock-like leaves; Pliny's britannica, usually a water dock; uncertain.
Willow-like leaves, purple or golden flowers, wet places; probably conflates Lysimachia and Lythrum.

Mountain plant with bay-like leaves; Solomon's seal (named from it).

Unidentified; Linnaeus's Polemonium borrows the name only, description does not clearly fit.

Grain-field weed with rue-like leaves, poppy-like juice; Hypecoum.

Fleawort; Plantago psyllium (=P. afra).
Edible garden strychnos; black nightshade.

Jointed fennel-like stem, heavy smell; poison hemlock.

Ephemeron/wild iris with lily-like leaves, small white flowers, woods; Convallaria proposed.
Parthenion/helxine; pellitory; Greek plant likely P. judaica.
Mouse-ear-leaved low herb of shady groves smelling of cucumber; chickweed.
